fine_lines.title: What does X mean? vs What do you mean?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: What does X mean? = اشرح لي معنى هذه الكلمة. What do you mean? = اشرح لي ما تقصده أنت (أفكارك).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "What does X mean?" = explain this word. "What do you mean?" = explain what you are trying to say.

examples.sentence: What do you mean, you can't come?

fine_lines.title: When do you use it? vs When would you use it?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: When do you use it? تسأل عن السياق الصحيح العام. When would you use it? تسأل الشخص عن تجربته الشخصية: متى تستعمله أنت؟
fine_lines.explanation_en: "When do you use it?" asks for the correct context in general. "When would you use it?" asks the person about their own use.

examples.sentence: Teacher, when would you use this word?

fine_lines.title: How long have you been here? vs How long will you stay?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: have been يسأل عن الزمن الذي مضى: I have been here for two weeks. will / going to يسأل عن المستقبل: I will stay for another two weeks / two more weeks.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Have been" asks about time until now: "I have been here for two weeks." "Will / going to" asks about the future: "I will stay for another two weeks / two more weeks."

examples.sentence: I have been in Canada for six months.
I'm going to stay here for six more weeks.

grammar.title: Question form: verb before subject
grammar.explanation_ar: في الإنجليزية يأتي الفعل (أو الفعل المساعد) قبل الفاعل في السؤال: Is it...? Are you...? وفي سؤال المعلومات: أداة الاستفهام + فعل مساعد + فاعل + الفعل الرئيسي.
grammar.explanation_en: In English questions, the verb (or helping verb) comes before the subject: Is it...? Are you...? Information questions: question word + helping verb + subject + main verb.

grammar.title: "What means X?" is wrong
grammar.explanation_ar: خطأ شائع: What means X? الصحيح: What does X mean? لأن المضارع البسيط يحتاج do/does في السؤال، ولا نضع فعلين معًا، فيصبح الفعل mean بدون s بعد الفاعل.
grammar.explanation_en: A common mistake: "What means X?" Correct: "What does X mean?" The simple present needs do/does in questions, and "mean" goes after the subject without -s.

grammar.title: Answer with the same tense
grammar.explanation_ar: أجب بنفس الزمن المستخدم في السؤال. How long have you been here? → I have been here for... (زمن مضى). How long will you stay? → I will stay for another... / I'm going to stay for ... more (مستقبل). How long will you have been here? → I will have been here for... (المدة الإجمالية). لا تقل two plus weeks.
grammar.explanation_en: Answer with the same tense as the question. "How long have you been here?" → "I have been here for..." (time until now). "How long will you stay?" → "I will stay for another... / I'm going to stay for ... more" (future). "How long will you have been here?" → "I will have been here for..." (total time). Don't say "two plus weeks".
examples: I have been here for two weeks.
I will stay here for another two weeks.
Next week, I will have been here for six months.
